title: Geometric-stalk test for Tor amplitude of an arbitrary ring sheaf on a space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$, with its small etale site [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $R$ be any sheaf of commutative rings on this site, not necessarily the structure sheaf, and $E\in D(R)$, the unbounded derived category of $R$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Compute derived tensors by K-flat resolutions. For a geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$, where $\Omega$ is algebraically closed, let $R_{\bar x}$ and $E_{\bar x}$ be the stalk ring and termwise stalk complex, formed over pointed etale scheme neighbourhoods. Geometric stalk functors on $R$-module sheaves are exact and jointly detect zero objects. For integers $a\le b$, the following conditions are equivalent: $H^i(E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M)=0$ for every $R$-module sheaf $M$ in degree zero and every $i\notin[a,b]$; and $H^i(E_{\bar x}\otimes_{R_{\bar x}}^{\mathbf L}N)=0$ for every geometric point $\bar x$, every $R_{\bar x}$-module $N$ in degree zero, and every $i\notin[a,b]$. This equivalence applies also after restriction to any etale scheme chart of $X$. No quasi-coherence, boundedness, Noetherian or quasi-compactness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0DJJ (lemma-tor-amplitude-stalk), both clauses; enough geometric points and exactness from spaces-properties.tex Tag 04K5 (theorem-exactness-stalks), applied to underlying abelian sheaves.

proof.text: For each $\bar x$, realize its geometric stalk as the inverse image of the point $p_{\bar x}$, and take its normalized ring/module presentation. The transported ring is exactly $R_{\bar x}$ and the transported module is the pointed-neighbourhood stalk with its induced action, by the underlying-set identifications in the presentation. The module functor is exact. It jointly detects zero module sheaves: apply the conservative geometric-stalk theorem to the underlying set map $M\to0$; an isomorphism there is a bijective module homomorphism, whose inverse is automatically linear. Thus a module sheaf is zero precisely when all its geometric stalks are zero.

source.place: Tag 0DJJ (lemma-tor-amplitude-stalk), points in the proof; spaces-properties.tex Tags 04K0 (lemma-stalk-gives-point) and 04K5 (theorem-exactness-stalks).

proof.text: Assume the sheaf Tor condition. The ringed-site flat-model criterion supplies a representative $P\simeq E$ with flat terms, zero outside $[a,b]$. The normalized point functor sends every term to a flat $R_{\bar x}$-module. Exactness from step 1, and the exact-functor cohomology comparison, show that the localized complex $P_{\bar x}$ represents $E_{\bar x}$. It is bounded above and flat, hence is K-flat over the stalk ring. For any $R_{\bar x}$-module $N$, the ordinary-module K-flat tensor computation identifies $E_{\bar x}\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{R_{\bar x}}N$ with the localization of $\operatorname{Tot}(P_{\bar x}\otimes N[0])$. Its degree $i$ term is $P^i_{\bar x}\otimes N$, zero for $i\notin[a,b]$, so its cohomology vanishes there. This tests every $N$, without assuming it is a stalk of a global sheaf.

source.place: Tag 0DJJ (lemma-tor-amplitude-stalk), forward implication via Tag 08H5 (lemma-tor-amplitude-pullback), expanded using Tag 08G1 (lemma-tor-amplitude); more-algebra.tex bounded-flat K-flat and derived tensor computation.

proof.text: For the converse assume all the stalk Tor conditions, and fix an arbitrary $R$-module sheaf $M$. Choose flat-term K-flat resolutions $P\to E$ (of a representative) and $Q\to M[0]$. Their total tensor represents $E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M$. By the K-flat stalk theorem, $P_{\bar x}$ and $Q_{\bar x}$ are K-flat; their terms remain flat by the flat-stalk theorem. Step 1 and the exact-functor cohomology comparison show that they represent $E_{\bar x}$ and $M_{\bar x}[0]$. The signed total-tensor stalk comparison identifies $(\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R Q))_{\bar x}$ with $\operatorname{Tot}(P_{\bar x}\otimes_{R_{\bar x}}Q_{\bar x})$. The ordinary-module K-flat tensor computation therefore gives a derived isomorphism $(E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M)_{\bar x}\simeq E_{\bar x}\otimes_{R_{\bar x}}^{\mathbf L}M_{\bar x}$. Applying the exact-functor cohomology comparison gives $H^i(E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M)_{\bar x}\cong H^i(E_{\bar x}\otimes_{R_{\bar x}}^{\mathbf L}M_{\bar x})$.

source.place: Tag 0DJJ (lemma-tor-amplitude-stalk), converse displayed equality; expanded with Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 0DEN (lemma-check-K-flat-stalks) and 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product).

proof.text: If $i\notin[a,b]$, the right side of the final comparison in step 3 is zero by the hypothesis applied to the particular module $N=M_{\bar x}$. Hence every stalk of $H^i(E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M)$ is zero. Step 1 gives $H^i(E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M)=0$. Since $M$ and $i$ were arbitrary, this proves the sheaf Tor condition.

For an etale scheme chart $U\to X$, the localized site $X_{\mathrm{et}}/U$ is $U_{\mathrm{et}}$. An object of $X_{\mathrm{et}}/U$ is a scheme $T$ with an etale map $h_T\to X$ and a map $f:T\to U$ over $X$. Then $f$ is etale: by the definition of etale maps to $X$, $W=T\times_XU$ is a scheme whose projections $W\to T$ and $W\to U$ are etale. The graph $\gamma=(\mathrm{id},f):T\to W$ satisfies $\mathrm{pr}_T\circ\gamma=\mathrm{id}_T$, so $\gamma$ is etale by etale cancellation, and $f=\mathrm{pr}_U\circ\gamma$ is etale as a composite. Conversely, if $T\to U$ is etale, then $T\to X$ is etale: for every scheme $T'\to X$, $T'\times_XT=(T'\times_XU)\times_UT$ is a scheme, etale over the etale $T'$-scheme $T'\times_XU$, hence etale over $T'$ as a composite. Maps and jointly surjective etale covering families agree on both sides. The same definition identifies $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ with the small etale site of the algebraic space $h_U$. The restricted ring sheaf is an arbitrary commutative ring sheaf on this site, and the restricted complex is an object of its unbounded module derived category. Apply steps 1--4 with the algebraic space represented by $U$ and this ring and complex. This proves exactly the same equivalence after restriction, with no additional hypothesis. If $U$ or $X$ is empty, the conservative-stalk theorem says its sheaf topos is trivial, so both conditions still hold.
